chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man makes a bequest to his brother while he is absent, it is not permissible for him to return the bequest to him, because if he were present and refused to accept it, he would seek someone else."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a bequest made to an heir who is currently absent?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to clarify that an absent heir’s inability to physically accept the bequest does not invalidate it, preserving the testator’s intent. This principle ensures that the bequest remains binding and effective, preventing the estate from being redistributed prematurely as if the heir had explicitly refused. It underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of legal obligations even when the beneficiary is not present to formally receive them.
